title: LCZ696 (Sac/Val) protects against high-fat diet-induced kidney injury in mice by targeting ROCK2 to suppress ROCK2/NF-kappaB signaling.
authors: Wang, Wenhan; Huang, Yingying; Guo, Xiaochen; Cao, Zhenyang; Jiang, Huifeng; Zheng, Qianrong; Shi, Shanzhen; Huang, Pan; Zhou, Jianghua; Hu, Feifei; Qian, Jinfu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究LCZ696药物通过靶向ROCK2/NF-kB信号通路保护高脂饮食诱导的肾损伤，属于药物-蛋白互作与疾病机制研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity-related kidney disease (ORKD) is an increasingly prevalent cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) worldwide, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. LCZ696 (sacubitril/valsartan, Sac/Val), an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, has demonstrated cardio-renal benefits; however, its role and underlying mechanism in ORKD remain unclear. METHODS: A high-fat diet (HFD)-induced murine model and palmitate (PA)-stimulated NRK-52E cells were used to evaluate the renoprotective effects of LCZ696. Renal function, histopathology, and fibrosis were assessed by biochemical and histological analyses. Transcriptomic sequencing followed by functional enrichment, kinase analysis, molecular docking, and biochemical experiment were performed to identify key regulatory pathways. Mechanistic validation was conducted through ROCK2 overexpression. RESULTS: LCZ696 (Sac/Val) administration significantly improved renal function and alleviated interstitial fibrosis in HFD-fed mice. Transcriptomic analyses identified ROCK2/NF-kappaB signaling as a potential key pathway. LCZ696 suppressed PA- and HFD-induced activation of ROCK2, as evidenced by reduced MYPT1 phosphorylation, inhibition of IkappaBalpha degradation, decreased nuclear accumulation of NF-kappaB P65, and downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines. ROCK2 overexpression largely reversed these effects, supporting its functional involvement. Molecular docking predicted stable binding of Sac and Val within the ROCK2 pocket, which was further supported by CETSA, DARTS, and pull-down assays. CONCLUSIONS: LCZ696 (Sac/Val) exerts anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects in ORKD, at least in part, through modulation of the ROCK2/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. These findings identify ROCK2-dependent inflammatory signaling as a potential therapeutic target and suggest that LCZ696 may represent a promising strategy for the treatment of ORKD.
abstract_zh: 背景：肥胖相关肾病（obesity-related kidney disease, ORKD）是全球范围内慢性肾脏病（chronic kidney disease, CKD）日益普遍的病因，然而有效的治疗策略仍然有限。LCZ696（沙库巴曲/缬沙坦，Sac/Val），一种血管紧张素受体-脑啡肽酶抑制剂，已显示出心肾益处；但其在ORKD中的作用及潜在机制尚不清楚。方法：采用高脂饮食（high-fat diet, HFD）诱导的小鼠模型和棕榈酸（palmitate, PA）刺激的NRK-52E细胞，评估LCZ696的肾脏保护作用。通过生化和组织学分析评估肾功能、组织病理学和纤维化。进行转录组测序，随后进行功能富集、激酶分析、分子对接和生化实验，以识别关键调控通路。通过ROCK2过表达进行机制验证。结果：LCZ696（Sac/Val）给药显著改善了HFD喂养小鼠的肾功能，并减轻了间质纤维化。转录组分析将ROCK2/NF-kappaB信号传导识别为潜在关键通路。LCZ696抑制了PA和HFD诱导的ROCK2激活，表现为MYPT1磷酸化减少、IkappaBalpha降解抑制、NF-kappaB P65核积累降低以及促炎细胞因子下调。ROCK2过表达在很大程度上逆转了这些效应，支持其功能参与。分子对接预测Sac和Val在ROCK2口袋内稳定结合，这进一步得到CETSA、DARTS和pull-down实验的支持。结论：LCZ696（Sac/Val）在ORKD中发挥抗炎和抗纤维化作用，至少部分通过调节ROCK2/NF-kappaB信号通路实现。这些发现将ROCK2依赖性炎症信号传导识别为潜在治疗靶点，并提示LCZ696可能代表一种有前景的ORKD治疗策略。
